subject: chemistry
title: Periodicity Adventure 1: Periodic trends — radius, IE, electronegativity
welcome_lead: Today you'll trend across the periodic table — Mendeleev's masterpiece.
meta_desc: Chemistry — periodic trends, atomic radius, ionisation energy, electronegativity.
final_note: You learned atomic radius decreases across, IE and electronegativity increase across; all reverse down a group.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mendeleev (1869) ordered elements by mass and properties, leaving gaps that predicted Ga, Ge, Sc.

Modern table orders by atomic number Z. Groups (vertical) share valence configuration; periods (horizontal) share principal shell.

S-block (groups 1-2), p-block (13-18), d-block (3-12), f-block (lanthanides/actinides).

Across period 3 (Na → Ar):

- Atomic radius ↓ (more protons, same shell pulls in).
- IE ↑ (harder to remove e⁻).
- Electronegativity ↑ (atom pulls bonding e⁻ harder).

Sudden falls between groups 2→13 (filling new sub-shell) and 15→16 (paired electron repulsion).

Down group 1 (Li → Cs):

- Atomic radius ↑ (more shells).
- IE ↓ (outer e⁻ further; shielding).
- Electronegativity ↓ (weaker pull).
- Reactivity ↑ (easier to lose e⁻).

Group 7 (halogens) — reactivity ↓ down group (e⁻ harder to attract from distance).

mcqs.q: If a complex ion has a coordination number of 4, what shape does it have?
options: The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
A coordination number of 4 always means tetrahedral, because that gives the maximum bond-angle separation.
A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
It can be either tetrahedral OR square planar — the shape depends on the metal and ligands (e.g. [Pt(NH3)4]2+ is square planar; [CuCl4]2- is tetrahedral).

mcqs.q: For a process to be spontaneous, what must happen to the total entropy of the universe?
options: The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
The entropy of the system must increase for the process to be spontaneous.
It must increase (ΔS_total > 0) — the system's entropy alone can decrease as long as the surroundings' entropy increases more.

mcqs.q: Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.
Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
